nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-01.title: Powers of two
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-01.body:
A set with $n$ elements has $2^n$ subsets, so we need $2^m-2^k=96$. Writing $2^k(2^{m-k}-1)=96=2^5\cdot3$ forces $k=5$ and $2^{m-k}-1=3$, so $m=7$: $128-32=96$.

**Answer: 7**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-02.title: Half the rectangle
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-02.body:
Triangle $AXD$ has base $AD$ and height equal to the rectangle's width, so its area is half the rectangle's. Since $5^2+12^2=13^2$, the triangle is right-angled at $X$ with area $\frac12\cdot5\cdot12=30$. The rectangle's area is $60$.

**Answer: 60**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-03.title: Combine exponents
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-03.body:
$x\sqrt[3]x=\sqrt[3]{x^4}$, so the left side is $\sqrt{\sqrt[3]{x^4}}$. For $x>0$ this is $x^{4/6}=x^{2/3}=64$, so $x=64^{3/2}=8^3=512$.

Note that $x=-512$ also works: $x\sqrt[3]x=(-512)(-8)=4096$ and $\sqrt{4096}=64$. The league's correction letter accepts $512$, $-512$, or both.

**Answer: 512**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-04.title: Inclusion-exclusion
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-04.body:
Measured from the $1$-inch mark, the $\frac1{24}$ marks are $\frac0{24},\dots,\frac{24}{24}$: $25$ marks. The $\frac19$ marks are $\frac09,\dots,\frac99$: $10$ marks. A mark is in both lists when it is a multiple of $\frac13$ (the lcm of $\frac19$ and $\frac1{24}$ in this sense): $0,\frac13,\frac23,1$, which is $4$ marks. Total $25+10-4=31$.

**Answer: 31**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-05.title: Pigeonhole
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-05.body:
With six eggs the bunny could have exactly two of each color and no triple. The seventh egg must make a third of some color.

**Answer: 7**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-06.title: Isosceles triangles
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-06.body:
Since $XY\parallel AB$, $\angle AMX=\angle MAB$, and since $AM$ bisects $\angle A$, $\angle MAB=\angle XAM$. So triangle $AXM$ is isosceles with $XM=AX=3$. Similarly $YM=BY=5$. Hence $XY=3+5=8$.

**Answer: 8**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-07.title: Largest divisor
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-07.body:
$x+3$ must divide $24$; the largest value is $x+3=24$, giving $x=21$.

**Answer: 21**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-09.title: Add the sides
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-09.body:
$3(x^2+y^2)+4(x^2-y^2)=7x^2-y^2$. (The problem calls the seven-sided polygon a "hexagon"; this does not affect the answer.)

**Answer: $7x^2-y^2$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-10.title: Count adjacent pairs
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-10.body:
The sheet is a $5\times5$ grid. Adjacent pairs: $5$ rows with $4$ horizontal pairs each and $5$ columns with $4$ vertical pairs each, $40$ in all. There are $\binom{25}2=300$ pairs of stamps, so the probability is $\frac{40}{300}=\frac2{15}$.

**Answer: $\frac{2}{15}$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-11.title: Middle term
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-11.body:
The terms are $1,r,r^2,r^3,r^4$ with $r^4=5$, so $r^2=\sqrt5$. The product is $r^{0+1+2+3+4}=r^{10}=(r^2)^5=(\sqrt5)^5=25\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $25\sqrt5$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-12.title: Distances from the centers
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-12.body:
The common chord is perpendicular to the line of centers. Let its foot be at distance $d$ from the center of the small circle and $10-d$ from the other, with half-chord $h$: $d^2+h^2=25$, $(10-d)^2+h^2=81$. Subtracting, $100-20d=56$, so $d=\frac{11}5$ and $h^2=25-\frac{121}{25}=\frac{504}{25}$, $h=\frac{6\sqrt{14}}5$. The chord is $2h=\frac{12\sqrt{14}}5$.

**Answer: $\frac{12\sqrt{14}}{5}$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-12.title: Area of the center triangle
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-12.body:
The two centers and one chord endpoint form a triangle with sides $5,9,10$. By Heron, $s=12$ and its area is $\sqrt{12\cdot7\cdot3\cdot2}=6\sqrt{14}$. Its height to the side of length $10$ is the half-chord: $\frac{2\cdot6\sqrt{14}}{10}=\frac{6\sqrt{14}}5$. The chord is $\frac{12\sqrt{14}}5$.

**Answer: $\frac{12\sqrt{14}}{5}$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-13.title: Sets of three coins
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-13.body:
One penny, one nickel and one quarter are worth $31$ cents, and $124=4\cdot31$, so he has $4$ of each, $12$ coins in all.

**Answer: 12**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-14.title: Convert to base ten
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-14.body:
In base nine, $10_9=9$, $13_9=12$, $15_9=14$. So the fractions are $\frac9{12}=\frac34$ and $\frac7{14}=\frac12$, with sum $\frac54$. The digits $5$ and $4$ mean the same in base seven, so the answer is $5/4$.

**Answer: $5/4$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-15.title: Side ratios
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-15.body:
With legs $p,q$ opposite $P,Q$ and hypotenuse $r$: $\sin P=\cos Q=\frac pr$ and $\sin Q=\cos P=\frac qr$, so the sum is $\frac{p^2+q^2}{r^2}=1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-16.title: Two right triangles
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-16.body:
Let the distances from the center to the chords be $d_1$ (6-inch chord) and $d_2$ (14-inch chord), with $d_1+d_2=10$. Then $r^2=9+d_1^2=49+d_2^2$, so $d_1^2-d_2^2=40$, i.e. $(d_1-d_2)\cdot10=40$ and $d_1-d_2=4$. Thus $d_1=7$ and $r^2=9+49=58$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{58}$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-18.title: Common external tangent
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-18.body:
Since $7-4<8<7+4$, the circles intersect, so the common tangent is external. $OX$ and $PY$ are both perpendicular to $XY$; drawing a line from $P$ parallel to $XY$ forms a right triangle with hypotenuse $OP=8$ and leg $7-4=3$. So $XY=\sqrt{64-9}=\sqrt{55}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{55}$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-19.title: Undo the markup
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-19.body:
The red dress sold for $0.9\cdot50=45$ dollars. The green dress's original price $g$ satisfies $1.1g=45$, so $g=\frac{450}{11}\approx40.91$, which is $41$ to the nearest dollar.

**Answer: 41 dollars**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-20.title: Solve for the terms
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-20.body:
With first term $a$ and difference $d$: $3(a+2d)=6(a+5d)$, so $3a+24d=0$ and $a+8d=0$. The ninth term is $a+8d=0$, so nine times it is $0$.

**Answer: 0**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-21.title: Law of cosines
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-21.body:
The angle between the rays is $\frac{4\pi}3$, so $AB^2=4^2+6^2-2\cdot4\cdot6\cos\frac{4\pi}3=52+24=76$ and $AB=2\sqrt{19}$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{19}$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-22.title: Split by an altitude
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-22.body:
The altitude to the side $14$ splits it into $5$ and $9$ ($5^2+12^2=13^2$, $9^2+12^2=15^2$), so the height is $12$ and the area is $\frac12\cdot14\cdot12=84$.

**Answer: 84**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-24.title: Man-days
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-24.body:
$4\cdot2=8$ man-days paint $3$ houses, so one man-day paints $\frac38$ house. In $5$ days, $x$ men paint $y=\frac{15x}{8}$ houses. Since $\gcd(15,8)=1$, $y$ is an integer exactly when $8\mid x$; the least is $x=8$ (then $y=15$).

**Answer: 8**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-26.title: Similar triangle at the top
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-26.body:
The part above $y=k$ is a triangle similar to $ABC$ with apex $B$ and height $6-k$ (out of $6$). Its area is half, so the ratio of similarity is $\frac1{\sqrt2}$: $6-k=\frac6{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt2$, giving $k=6-3\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $6-3\sqrt2$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-27.title: Inverse functions
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-27.body:
$g$ is the inverse of $f$: if $y=\frac1{1-x}$ then $1-\frac1y=x$. So $f(g(t))=g(f(t))=t$ and the difference is $0$.

**Answer: 0**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-29.title: Use the angle between 2 and 5
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-29.body:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between the sides $2$ and $5$. Then $x=\text{Area}=5\sin\theta$ and $x^2=29-20\cos\theta$. So $25\sin^2\theta=29-20\cos\theta$, i.e. $25\cos^2\theta-20\cos\theta+4=0$, $(5\cos\theta-2)^2=0$, $\cos\theta=\frac25$. Then $x^2=29-8=21$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{21}$**

nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-30.title: Set up the ratio
nyciml-1989-90-spring-seniorb-30.body:
Let each candle burn $r$ inches per minute. At 2:00 PM, $A$ has burned $140$ minutes and $B$ $100$; at 3:00 PM, $200$ and $160$. So
$$\frac{10-200r}{10-160r}=\frac12\cdot\frac{10-140r}{10-100r}.$$
Cross-multiplying: $2(10-200r)(10-100r)=(10-140r)(10-160r)$, i.e. $200-6000r+40000r^2=100-3000r+22400r^2$, so $176r^2-30r+1=0$ and $r=\frac18$ or $r=\frac1{22}$. With $r=\frac18$, candle $A$ would be gone after $80$ minutes, before 2:00, so $r=\frac1{22}$. Candle $A$ lasts $220$ minutes from 11:40 AM, burning out at 3:20 PM.

Check: at 2:00 the lengths are $\frac{80}{22}$ and $\frac{120}{22}$ (ratio $\frac23$); at 3:00 they are $\frac{20}{22}$ and $\frac{60}{22}$ (ratio $\frac13$).

**Answer: 3:20 PM**
